# SPE round 3 plan

Round 3 tests one fix in config C, adds a harder ticket set, drops config D, and raises trials per cell to 5. In round 2 the naive guess beat my predictions on 4 of 5 rows and tied on 1. Every miss came from moving a number in the hopeful direction. This plan moves only one main-set number away from "same as last round".

Defaults I chose because the details are missing:
- The main ticket set is the same 30 tickets as round 2.
- The fixed config C is named **C2** in files.
- A prediction is a hit when it lands within ±0.01 of the measured value. I read this rule from the round 2 log.

## 1. Specify

### Decisions on the round 3 proposals

| ID | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | Adopt | F4 is the only failure with a known mechanism and a one-step fix. |
| P2 | Adopt, scored as a separate set | A and B sit at 0.86. Scoring the 10 new tickets apart from the main set keeps the main-set numbers comparable to round 2. |
| P3 | Adopt as a default, owner is the user | D cost more than predicted ($0.004 against $0.002), and F6 is still open. Cost is the only reason D exists. The other option is to keep D and cap Haiku retries at 1. |
| P4 | Adopt | B's miss of 0.02 is inside noise at n=3. Five trials per cell narrows that noise. |

### Requirements, round 3 (added to `spe/spec/spec.md`)

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R3-1 | C2 is C with the outage status check split back out as its own tool. Nothing else changes. | P1, r02 F4 | The dry run on r02-C-T17 shows a status-check call. The transcript scan counts status-check calls on every outage ticket in C2. |
| R3-2 | Add 10 hard tickets that mix billing and outage. Score them as their own set. | P2 | `hard-r03` has 10 tickets with gold labels. Results report the main set and the hard set separately. |
| R3-3 | Run configs A, B, and C2. D does not run. | P3, r02 F6 | The Workflow config list is exactly `["A","B","C2"]`. F6 is marked "parked, D dropped". |
| R3-4 | Run 5 trials per cell. | P4 | Every cell has at least 5 valid trials or a logged skip. |
| R3-5 | The grader reads `label.priority` and never reads the draft reply. | r02 F5 | A selftest case has a draft reply that says P1 and a label that says P2. That case must grade as P2. |
| R3-6 | Watch every config for the F6 retry pattern. | r02 F6 | Flag any trial whose token count is more than 2 times its cell median. |
| R3-7 | A and B are unchanged controls. | Decision | Their config hashes match round 2. |

### Logged in `spe/spec/disagreements.md`

| # | Item | Default | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Drop D, or keep D with a retry cap | Drop D | User |
| D2 | I write the gold labels for the 10 hard tickets | I write them. They are scored apart from the main set, and I list each label in the results commit for review. | User |
| D3 | The verdict rule stays at ±0.01, which is very tight for a 10-ticket set | Keep the rule. Report a 95% interval next to each measured value. Revisit in r04. | User |
| D4 | No same-round C control | A and B are the drift controls. r02 C is the C2 baseline. | Claude |
| D5 | C's category accuracy fell from 0.84 to 0.80, and no failure type explains it | Leave it open. The failure analysis looks for a cause. | Claude |

There is one small log fix for the specify commit. In the round 2 A row, the prediction (0.85) was 0.01 off and the naive guess (0.84) was 0.02 off. The Closer should say "predicted", not "tie". I will check the tie rule first. If the label is wrong, I will correct it with a dated note.

## 2. Predict

The starting point is "same as last round", from `spe/predictions/r03-draft.yaml` and the round 2 log. Category is graded by exact match on `label.category`. Priority is graded by exact match on `label.priority`. Both checks live in `grade.py`.

### Main set (30 tickets, 5 trials per cell)

| Metric | A | B | C2 | Same as last round | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| category accuracy | 0.86 | 0.86 | 0.80 | A 0.86, B 0.86, C 0.80 | A and B did not change. C2 changes only the outage tool, and no round 2 evidence links F4 to category errors. |
| priority accuracy | n/a | n/a | 0.76 | C 0.71 | F4 sent outage tickets to P3. Splitting the check out brings back the lookup. I move only partway toward r01's 0.78 because r01 was graded before the F5 fix, and I have not yet counted the outage tickets. |

### Hard set (10 tickets, 5 trials per cell, measured for the first time)

| Metric | A | B | C2 | Naive guess (main-set value) | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| category accuracy | 0.70 | 0.70 | 0.65 | A 0.86, B 0.86, C2 0.80 | A mixed ticket has two plausible categories, so I expect more errors. C2 starts lower because C was lower on the main set. |

Cost per ticket is a budget line this round and is not predicted. Round 2 predicted cost only for D, and D is dropped.

## 3. Evaluate

### Gates (all must pass before launch)

1. **Grader selftest.** The oracle answers pass. Empty answers fail. Wrong answers fail. The F5 case from R3-5 grades correctly.
2. **Control regrade.** Regrade the round 2 transcripts with the current `grade.py`. The results must match the round 2 regraded numbers exactly: A 0.86, B 0.86, C 0.80, C priority 0.71. If they do not match, I halt and report. I also regrade r01 priority and record its old and new numbers side by side.
3. **Dry run on 3 cells.** C2 on r02-C-T17 for 2 trials. A on 1 hard ticket for 1 trial. B on 1 main ticket for 1 trial. Each trial must pass the schema. The C2 trial must call the status check. The peek scan must come back clean.

### Run

- `ROUND = 3` is set once as a constant in `spe/evals/harness/r03-workflow.js`. No prompt text has a round number typed in by hand.
- Each trial returns a schema with `category`, `priority`, `tool_calls`, and `tokens`. Code checks do all the grading. No judge is needed this round.
- Hard-set gold labels live in `spe/evals/grader/labels/hard-r03.jsonl`. Trials cannot read that directory.
- After the run, I scan each transcript for reads of the grader, the labels, or `spe/predictions/`. Any trial that peeked is void.
- A split cell is a cell whose trials disagree. Each split cell gets up to 3 extra trials.
- The run ends with a failure analysis and a completeness critic. The failure analysis covers D5 and any R3-6 flags.

### Workflow arguments

```js
{
  ROUND: 3,
  configs: ["A", "B", "C2"],
  sets: { main: "spe/evals/tickets/main.jsonl", hard: "spe/evals/tickets/hard-r03.jsonl" },
  trialsPerCell: 5,
  extraTrialsCap: 3,
  maxTrials: 720,
  budgetUsd: 40
}
```

### Cost estimate (not measured)

- The base run is 3 configs × 40 tickets × 5 trials, which is 600 trials. Split-cell extras bring the most it can reach to 720 trials. The dry run adds 4 trials.
- I assume about $0.04 per trial for A, B, and C2. That is 10 times D's measured $0.004, because D was the cheap-model config.
- The estimate is about $24 for the base run and about $29 at the most. The cap is $40. The harness skips any trial that would cross the cap and logs the skip. I halt and report if the cap is reached.

## 4. After approval, in order

1. Save "ok, next one" verbatim to `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r03.md`. Add the R3 table, the P1 to P4 decisions, and D1 to D5. Commit `SPE r03 specify`.
2. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r03.md`. Write `spe/predictions/r03.yaml`. It starts with `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` and holds the round, the date, the author ("Claude, approved by the user in plan mode"), the configs, every number above with its Why, and `same_as_last_round`. Leave `r03-draft.yaml` unchanged. Commit `SPE r03 predict: C2 priority 0.76, hard set added, D dropped`.
3. Write the 10 hard tickets and their labels, write C2, and write the harness. Run the gates. Commit `SPE r03 evaluate (harness)`.
4. Launch the Workflow. Close out when the completion notice arrives. Commit `SPE r03 evaluate (results): <headline>`.
5. Learn. Update the prediction log with "Which Why broke", and say plainly if the naive guess won again. Add new F-numbered failures with original and regraded numbers side by side. Add "Proposed for round 4" to the spec, write `r04-draft.yaml`, and update `spe/README.md`. Commit `SPE r03 learn` and tag `spe-r03`.

All commits stay local. Nothing is pushed.

## Stop and halt checks

- The stop rule needs 3 matching rounds in a row. Round 2 matched on 1 of 5 rows, so the loop continues.
- I halt and report on any of these: the $40 cap is hit, the control regrade does not match, a trial reads the labels, or a decision only the user can make blocks the run.
